Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Traffic and Safety Committee  Members  will  be
participating via teleconference. Committee meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
882 4383 6788 Passcode: 630708 (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 882 4383 6788 Passcode: 630708.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  AUGUST 17, 2021

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Martin, Munday,
  Romanelli, Brown Schachter, Scott

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Combs, Lum, Varner

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Bouse, LA County Sheriff’s Department

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MAY 4, 2021.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN
to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MAY 4, 2021.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  3717 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH - ADDRESS NUMBER

Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy stated that this item is being presented per a request
of several residents of 3717, 3719 and 3721 Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN). Exhibits were
presented with photos of the existing address signage. The original request was for the large
street name sign similar to those posted for cross streets along PVDN. However, the location of
the sign would conflict with the Dobbin Lane sign putting the sign too close to the street entrance.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she spoke to staff at Rolling Hills and obtained the
dimensions for the signs along PVDN. A sample of the address sign, which could be created for
the City of Rolling Hills Estates’ properties was presented.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the specific need for the address sign for 3717, 3719 and 3721 PVDN; discuss
the overall need for address signs for properties having direct access to Palos Verdes Drive North.
This may include policy/guideline for staff to follow when such requests are made. The exact
policy/guidelines can be brought back to the Committee for final review and approval.

Randall Harwood, 3719 PVDN, stated that the Dobbin Lane sign has confused guests visiting
their home. His request is for a similar sign with the three addresses and an arrow pointing to their
driveway. Mr. Harwood stated that he is requesting this particularly for emergency vehicles to be
able to find their addresses. He stated that emergency vehicles have driven by without being able
to locate 3717 PVDN. Mr. Harwood stated that he is requesting address signs visible to those
traveling east and westbound.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI, Deputy Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that this was requested by Mr. Palacios as a result of an incident where emergency
services vehicles had trouble finding address 3717 Palos Verdes Drive North. Deputy Engineering

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, August 17, 2021
 Deputy Itagaki stated that the concern with providing the large street name sign is that these are
generally used for streets where this is a shared driveway. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI
expressed his concern with setting a precedence for similar requests. He stated that in his own
experience with a similar situation, he took personal action to make sure that the street sign
indicate the addresses on the private road where he lives. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI
stated that there is a need, but this would set a precedence for similar requests.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN described a similar incident on his street and expressed his
concern with responding agencies being unable to find an address. He stated that due to the
safety aspect, he would like to see the addresses for that street be visible.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that the individual address signs for
Rolling Hills on PVDN work well. She stated that the example shown with the City of Rolling Hills
logo on a similar sign would work well and added that the signs do not need to have names and
the fonts should be consistent. She stated that she does not think that the large sign is necessary,
but a sign on the north side visible to emergency vehicles is necessary.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked for clarification on a similar sign for 3739 through 3815
PVDN. Director Wahba stated that the sign serves as a street sign for the ten homes on what is
known as “no name street”. The proposed request is for a hidden driveway where only 3717 is
visible from PVDN. However, the larger signs are reserved for street signs, but there is a need for
signage for these homes. COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that Mr. Harwood’s
preference would be for the larger sign on the westbound side of the street. Mrs. Harwood
explained that on the east side, they are not proposing a new sign and rather that the addresses
to be added onto the back of the existing sign for Dobbin Lane.

Mr. Vincent Di Piazza, 3717 PVDN, stated that in the last nine months he has had three instances
where paramedics were called to his residence. In the instances where he could go outside, he
had to flag the paramedics down with a flashlight to find his home, however, there was an instance
where he could not and depended on his kids to go out. A sign would be the best solution and it
needs to be a sign that will catch driver’s attention.

Mr. Darren Palacios, 3721 PVDN, stated that he sent the request to the City due to an incident
on the morning of June 9, 2021 where the Fire Department was called to his neighbors’ home.
Mr. Palacios stated that he was with the Fire Department for thirty seven years. The Fire
Department engineer and captain were very upset with being unable to find the home and
demanded that he go to the city to request street signage similar to that of 3739 through 3815
PVDN. Mr. Palacios stated that he is willing to pay the cost to move and install the Dobbin Lane
sign. He further questioned the staff report which states, “Relocation of the Dobbin Lane sign
would place the sign too close to the street entrance”. Mr. Palacios stated that various street
signs off of PVDN are 30 ft. or less from the street entrance. He also stated that the street sign
going east from Crenshaw to Rolling Hills Road; the sign for Rawhide Lane is 75 ft. from the street
entrance. He added that the sign for 3739 through 3815 have existing signs opposite their
driveways and stated that the Dobbin Lane sign is confusing for the addresses at 3717, 3719 and
3721 PVDN. Mr. Palacios stated that a property in Palos Verdes Estates has the same address
and zip code as his property and when he and his wife tested this with 911, they got Palos Verdes
Estates Police Department. This has since been corrected. Mr. Palacios further expressed his
concern with emergency services not being able to reach the homes on their street and stated
that a more prominent address sign is needed.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that the westbound side of the street is paved and a
sign could not be installed there. She stated that the logical solution would be to move the Dobbin
Lane sign further down the street and install a sign across from the street similar to those on
PVDN.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT thanked Mr. Palacios for his many years of service. He stated
that he previously thought that the driveway off of 3717 PVDN was for stables or horse property
in the rear of the property and learned otherwise when the Palacios’ purchased the home.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT inquired 3739 through 3815 PVDN are on a private or public
street. Director Wahba stated that it is a private street and there are ten homes on the street.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked how far the Dobbin Lane sign is from Dobbin Lane and
the standard for placement of those signs. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that it is
approximately 280 to 300 ft. from the street. Director Wahba stated that locating signs in the City

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, August 17, 2021
 sometimes depends on trees, curvature of the road, topography, etc.; standards may not be found
as they would for CalTrans, for example. Director Wahba stated that the Dobbin Lane sign may
be too far from the entrance and consideration may be given to move the sign. COMMITTEE
MEMBER SCOTT stated that a better location would be by the storm drain entrance and past the
3717 driveway moving east. This issue is about real emergencies and the Dobbin sign should be
moved since it is misleading. COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that the Dobbin Lane sign
can remain where it is and have it repainted on both sides with the addresses for 3717, 3719 and
3721 PVDN.

Director Wahba asked if the Committee would be in favor of placing the addresses on both sides
of the sign. COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT member stated that he is in favor of having the
addresses on both sides. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the Dobbin Lane sign
could remain and change it to the addresses for 3717, 3719 and 3721 PVDN and install a new
Dobbin Lane sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN
to,
  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO REPURPOSE THE DOBBIN
  LANE SIGN WITH THE ADDRESSES AT 3717, 3719 AND 3721 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH ON THE FRONT AND BACK AND INSTALL A NEW DOBBIN LANE SIGN EAST
  OF 3717 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH DRIVEWAY TO A POINT, DETERMINED BY
  STAFF, FOR DIRECTING TRAFFIC TO DOBBIN LANE.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Director Wahba stated that DigAlert will be
contacted to make sure that there are no utility lines in the area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that there should be a communication sent to the
residents on Dobbin Lane regarding this change.

The motion was amended as follows:

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN
to,
  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO REPURPOSE THE DOBBIN
  LANE SIGN WITH THE ADDRESSES AT 3717, 3719 AND 3721 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH ON THE FRONT AND BACK; INSTALL A NEW DOBBIN LANE SIGN EAST OF
  3717 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH DRIVEWAY TO A POINT, DETERMINED BY
  STAFF, FOR DIRECTING TRAFFIC TO DOBBIN LANE; AND, STAFF TO NOTIFY THE
  RESIDENTS OF DOBBIN LANE OF THIS CHANGE.

AYES: Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Scott
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Lum, Varner
ABSTAIN:

B.  MASONGATE DRIVE - EQUESTRIAN CROSSWALK

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that that there is a bridle trail behind the crosswalk at
Masongate Drive and there are existing signs upon entering and exiting Masongate. The results
of a review done on equestrian crossings along PVDN from Dapplegray Lane to Ponderosa Lane
was presented. The proposed Masongate equestrian crosswalk would be similar to the one at
City Hall. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested adding a “Trail Crossing Ahead” sign upon
exiting Masogate Drive and another “Trail Crossing” sign at the equestrian crosswalk.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the need for the equestrian crosswalk on Masongate Drive at Palos Verdes
Drive North and discuss the suggested traffic signs and pavement marking. It is further
recommended that the Committee receive public testimony and provide direction to staff
regarding the matter.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked what prompted this request. COMMITTEE
MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she brought this up at the last meeting and added that when
turning right, there are two trees that obstruct visibility to the horses coming up the trail.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, August 17, 2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she also received the same request
from Terry Griggs who is on the Equestrian Committee. She added that there is also a lot of brush
as you turn into Masongate Drive from PVDN, which blocks people, horses and bicyclists coming
out of the shadows. COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE added that there are two tree trunk,
bushes and a utility pole that obstruct visibility. COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that
he would be in favor of a crosswalk and clearance of overgrown brush to improve the visibility
and stated that he does not believe additional signage is necessary.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN stated that he lives on Sunnyfield where riders and drivers have
great visibility. He stated that clearing the brush would be an excellent idea for better visibility.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that she would like a “Trail Crossing” sign
added coming out from Masongate Drive since currently the only sign is for the Bike Trail and
inquired if there is a sign that has both, bike and equestrian trail crossing. Traffic Engineering
Deputy Itagaki stated that there is no sign with pedestrian, horse and bike crossing and suggested
that a “pedestrian/bike” sign and “trail crossing” sign be installed instead or only add the
equestrian sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that he agrees that there is a need for signs. He stated
that at the equestrian crosswalk further down on Masongate at Ferncreek, the curbs are not raised
and it catches your eye to someone/something that may come into the street. He inquired if
something similar could be done at this crosswalk. Director Wahba stated that this is something
that could be considered.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that the equestrian crosswalk is essential and it is quite
far from the pedestrian/bicycle crosswalk. Other than the equestrian sign, there is no other
indication that there is a crosswalk. In addition, the Eucalyptus, Pepper Tree and telephone pole
becomes an impediment to visibility and stated that he would support removing the Pepper Tree
and adding a crosswalk. He also stated that a better location for the equestrian sign would be
coming up from Masongate towards PVDN closer to the new crosswalk. He stated that he does
not think any additional signage is necessary.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she agrees with adding the equestrian crosswalk
and would support lowering the curbs after first checking on any potential drainage issues. She
also stated that she agrees with the removal of the Pepper Tree and removing the brush on the
other side. She stated that she is in favor of installing the “Trail Crossing” sign.

A brief discussion ensued regarding removal of the Pepper Tree.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN
SCHACHTER to,

  MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO ADD STRIPING FOR AN
  EQUESTRIAN CROSSWALK; RELOCATE THE SIGNS COMING UP FROM
  MASONGATE TO PVDN, MOVING THE EXISTING EQUESTRIAN SIGN OR ADDING A
  NEW “TRAIL CROSSING” SIGN TO THE LOCATION OF THE EXISTING BIKE SIGN
  AND MOVE THE BIKE SIGN FURTHER UP NEXT TO THE EXISTING CROSSWALK;
  REMOVE THE PEPPER TREE; AND, CLEAR THE BRUSH ON THE OTHER SIDE.
AYES: Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Scott
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Lum, Varner
ABSTAIN:

A brief discussion ensued regarding lowering the curb and the Committee agreed on two separate
motions.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI commented that the curb was not part of the initial
discussion and would not be in favor of a separate motion.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked if there is any policy that resulted whether there should
be curbs at horse crossings. Director Wahba stated that he has not seen a policy for curbs at
horse crossings and raised curbs vary from neighborhood to neighborhood. COMMITTEE
MEMBER SCOTT suggested referring this to the Equestrian Committee to determine if there
should be a policy on curbs at horse crossings.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, August 17, 2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO INVESTIGATE THE FEASIBILITY AND COST OF LOWERING THE
  CURBS TO STREET LEVEL ON BOTH SIDES OF THE EQUESTRIAN CROSSING ON
  MASONGATE DRIVE AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND IF FEASIBLE MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION TO THE CITY COUNCIL. IN ADDITION, ENLIST THE IDEAS OF
  THE EQUESTRIAN COMMUNITY REGARDING CURBS AT HORSE CROSSINGS.

AYES: Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Scott
NOES:
ABSENT: Combs, Lum, Varner
ABSTAIN:

C.  DAPPLEGRAY LANES SPEED HUMP SURVEY

Director Wahba stated that this item was prompted by the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners
Association (DLPOA) to have staff look at potential speed hump locations in addition to those that
exist on Dapplegray Lane. Staff worked with Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki to determine
potential speed hump locations. Over the summer a survey was sent out to all property owners
of the DLPOA. The City’s policy requires a simple majority or fifty plus one percent of the homes
on the street in order to approve the installation of speed humps. Director Wahba stated that this
was not reached on any of the three streets in the DLPOA.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked the Committee what they think about this policy. The way it is
currently, those who don’t vote are essentially voting “no” and stated that he is not sure it shouldn’t
be a matter of the simple majority. COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that due to his history
with RHCC, you will never get one hundred percent and those who did not vote will be upset if
the majority of those who did vote is accepted. He stated that a fifty plus one vote is more reflective
of it being an urgent need for the neighborhood.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that he supports the comments of Committee
Member Scott and stated that Los Ranchos Verdes had twenty five plus year old CC&Rs that
required two thirds approval of the homeowners who participate in the homeowners association;
this was amended to fifty plus one in order to be able to get a decision for any future projects.

This item was received and filed.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that he is in the Marloma development and he was
approached regarding taking a look at options for the Latigo Lane and Silver Spur/PVDN
intersection. When going westbound on PVDN, there are two lanes that merge into one and there
is concern that the driver in the right lane may not be paying attention to pedestrians when
crossing south across PVDN. There have been incidents where residents walking have been
nearly run over. COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY has suggested the feasibility of going back to
one lane. Director Wahba stated that this could be brought to the next Traffic and Safety
Committee meeting on November 2nd.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that he received a letter regarding young people riding electric trail
bikes on horse trails and zooming across intersections. He looked at the vehicle code and spoke
to the Sheriff along with the City Manager and the California Vehicle Code does have standards
for who can ride e-bikes. This may be an item that will need to be discussed in the future.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER asked for clarification on vehicles parked on the
street between three and five a.m. Even when these vehicles are called into the Sheriff’s
Department, it doesn’t seem that vehicles are being cited. She stated that one part of the street
turns and narrows and there was an instance when emergency vehicles could not get through
due to vehicles parked on both sides of the street. Deputy Bouse stated that tickets are written
when it is called in or suggested reporting it to the city and the morning deputies will be alerted to
check the area. Deputy Bouse stated that she will alert the morning deputies to check the area.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  5
Minutes, August 17, 2021
 CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that he spoke to deputies at National Night Out and received the
same response.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that several years ago there was approval for a stop line
for a median cut at Montecillo. There is a significant visibility problem for cars coming west and
turning north into Montecillo caused by a Eucalyptus Tree and would like to request that this one
be removed to improve visibility. This is the first Eucalyptus Tree east of the median cut. Director
Wahba requested that a picture be sent to him to address the issue.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that on lower Ferncreek there was a stop sign installed
so that the resident at the first house on Sugarhill on the right could get out of his driveway. There
is a safety concern with people driving through the stop sign since they know that there is no
enforcement at that intersection. Deputy Bouse stated that she will put a request to the two traffic
deputies on the Peninsula to monitor the area. COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she
would like to discuss the possibility of having the stop sign from Sugarhill going onto Masongate
removed. The stop sign on Ferncreek to Masongate should remain.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:02 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,

______________________________  _______________________________
